import json

)
LABEL_MAP = {1: "pass", 0: "fail"}

def load_jsonl(path):
    with open(path) as f:
        return [json.loads(line) for line in f]

def select_shots(train_data, n_pass=2, n_fail=1, seed=42):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    pass_examples = [ex for ex in train_data if ex["label"] == 1]
    fail_examples = [ex for ex in train_data if ex["label"] == 0]
    rng.shuffle(pass_examples)
    rng.shuffle(fail_examples)
    shots = pass_examples[:n_pass] + fail_examples[:n_fail]
    rng.shuffle(shots)
    return shots

def build_few_shot_user_msg(shots, query):
    parts = []
    for i, shot in enumerate(shots, 1):
        verdict = LABEL_MAP[shot["label"]]
        parts.append(
            f"Example {i}:\n## Code\n{shot['code']}\n\n## Test\n{shot['test']}\n\nVerdict: {verdict}"
        )
    parts.append(
        f"Now predict:\n## Code\n{query['code']}\n\n## Test\n{query['test']}\n\nVerdict:"
    )
    return "\n\n".join(parts)

    try:

    shots = select_shots(train_data, n_pass=2, n_fail=1, seed=args.seed)
    log.info(f"Selected {len(shots)} shots: {[LABEL_MAP[s['label']] for s in shots]}")

    log.info("Loading Qwen3-8B...")

```python
if len(ids) > args.max_seq_length:

```

The issue is it truncates from the right, which removes the generation prompt. The model then just continues from wherever it was truncated to, generating code instead of "pass"/"fail". 

The repo-level code + 3 shots is too long for 8192 tokens, so essentially ALL samples get truncated, and all the model generates is code continuation because the generation prompt (asking for "Verdict:") was cut off.


The few-shot examples themselves already exceed the token limit, so truncation happens within the shots before the query even gets included. Since every sample produces identical output, the model's defaulting to the majority class in the dataset, which explains why the 72.96% accuracy is just matching the base rate of passing samples.
